title: Exact worst-case counts and expected exact counts are different questions
statement: For A inertia(p, q, z), a maximal totally A-isotropic subspace has dimensionz+min(p, q); reading its complement and one residual linear direction supplies pointwise exact evaluation. Optimal HARD count is0 if A=b=0; rank A if A is semidefinite and b is in range A; rank A+1 if A is semidefinite and b is not in range A; max(p, q)+1 if A is indefinite. Terminal affine fibers give the matching lower bound, including zero-error almost-sure evaluation under a full-support Gaussian. This does NOT classify optimal expected exact count. Certified eigenvalue signs/exact-real observations are needed for exact classification; approximate-risk certificates can avoid an eigengap. Balanced inner product needsm+1 adaptive versus2m fixed exact reads, ratio tending2. Established inertia/isotropic/compression machinery is credited, not invented here.

requires: Known real quadratic and exact scalar linear measurements; hard worst-case count.
For almost-sure lower bound, the stated full-support Gaussian/conditional-fiber hypotheses and independent seed.
